title: Agent identity and the confused deputy

beats.narration: A valet key lets the valet drive your car, but not open the boot or the glovebox.
beats.on_screen: Illustration: a valet takes a car key; the key fob shows "valet key".

beats.narration: The key sets the limit, not the valet's request.
beats.on_screen: The valet tries the boot. It stays shut.

beats.narration: Here Alice is signed in. A hijacked planner asks for every customer anyway.
beats.on_screen: The lab, scenario 18. "The signed-in user is Alice (customer_id=1)." The planner asks for every customer.

beats.narration: The agent's database credential can read the whole table, so it uses its own power instead of Alice's. That is a confused deputy.
In secure mode the executor ignores the model's filter and binds the customer number from Alice's session. One row, hers.
beats.on_screen: Switch to **Secure**, run. `DEFENSE`: "executor discarded the model's filter and bound customer_id=1". SQL: 1 row. Caption: "Contained at EXECUTOR".

beats.narration: Notice the difference from the SQL injection fix. That one refused the call. Identity narrows it to the person signed in.
beats.on_screen: Side by side: SQL injection secure run (refused) and identity secure run (scoped to 1 row).

kw.title: Refuse vs scope
kw.body_text: SQL injection secure run refused the call. Identity narrows it to the person signed in — one row, Alice’s.

beats.narration: A valet key is a physical object. A session is data, so it has to be bound on the server, where the model cannot touch it.

kw.text: A valet key is a physical object. A session is data, so it has to be bound on the server, where the model cannot touch it.
